paperInfo.subject: Agric, Science & Tech
paperInfo.paperName: Grade 7 Agric, Science & Tech — Paper 2 (Practice Set A)

questions.questionText: SECTION A (30 marks - answer ALL questions in this section, about 75 minutes). Question 1 (5 marks): (a) List any two environmental factors that affect agriculture [2]. (b) Describe any one branch of agriculture [1]. (c) Give one profession in agriculture [1]. (d) Which department deals with crop protection (pests and diseases) in agriculture? [1]
questions.explanation: Model answer, written in the real ZIMSEC Grade 7 Agriculture Paper 2 structured format (original content, not copied from any real paper). (a) Any two: rainfall/climate, temperature, soil type, altitude, relief/topography (accept any two valid environmental factors). (b) Any one branch, described: e.g. Animal husbandry - the branch of agriculture concerned with the rearing and management of livestock such as cattle, goats and poultry for food and income. (c) Any one profession: e.g. Agricultural Extension Officer, Veterinarian, Agronomist, Soil Scientist. (d) The Plant Protection department (or Crop Protection/Plant Quarantine Services) deals with pests and diseases affecting crops.

questions.questionText: (5 marks): (a) Name two agents of physical (mechanical) weathering [2]. (b) What do the following terms mean: (i) soil fertility [1]; (ii) soil erosion [1]. (c) How does crop rotation improve soil fertility? [1]
questions.explanation: Model answer. (a) Any two agents of physical weathering: temperature change (expansion and contraction of rocks), frost action, wind, water/rain, action of plant roots growing into cracks. (b)(i) Soil fertility is the ability of soil to supply enough nutrients, water and air to support healthy plant growth. (ii) Soil erosion is the removal/washing or blowing away of the top layer of soil by water or wind. (c) Crop rotation improves soil fertility because growing different crops (e.g. alternating legumes with cereals) in sequence prevents the depletion of the same nutrients season after season, and legume crops such as beans add nitrogen to the soil through nitrogen-fixing bacteria in their root nodules.

questions.questionText: (5 marks): (a)(i) A rain gauge recorded the following monthly rainfall: January 45mm, February 60mm, March 35mm, April 20mm. Calculate the total rainfall for these four months [2]. (ii) Which instrument is used to measure rainfall? [1]. (b) What measures should a farmer take to protect crops against hailstorm damage? [2]
questions.explanation: Model answer. (a)(i) Total rainfall = 45 + 60 + 35 + 20 = 160mm. (ii) A rain gauge is used to measure rainfall. (b) Any two measures: use of hail nets/covers over crops; growing crops in greenhouses or under shelter; planting hail-resistant/quick-maturing varieties; taking out crop insurance against hail damage; timing planting to avoid the season when hailstorms are most common in the area.

questions.questionText: (5 marks): (a) What are pesticides? [1]. (b) Why should a farmer wear protective clothing when applying agro-chemicals? [2]. (c) What do the following colour codes on agro-chemical containers mean: (i) red [1]; (ii) blue? [1]
questions.explanation: Model answer. (a) Pesticides are chemicals used to kill or control pests (insects, weeds, fungi or other organisms) that damage crops or livestock. (b) Any two reasons: to protect the skin, eyes and lungs from direct contact with harmful chemicals; to prevent poisoning/chemical burns; to reduce the risk of the chemical being absorbed into the body and causing illness. (c)(i) Red indicates the agro-chemical is very toxic/highly poisonous/extremely dangerous, requiring the most caution. (ii) Blue indicates the agro-chemical is moderately hazardous.

questions.questionText: (5 marks): (a) What is malnutrition? [1]. (b) State one function of each of the following nutrients: (i) fats [1]; (ii) vitamins [1]. (c) Give one disease caused by a lack of: (i) vitamin C [1]; (ii) protein [1]
questions.explanation: Model answer. (a) Malnutrition is a condition caused by not eating a balanced diet - either eating too little of the right nutrients (undernutrition) or an unhealthy imbalance of nutrients. (b)(i) Fats provide the body with a concentrated source of energy and help absorb certain vitamins. (ii) Vitamins help protect the body against disease and keep body processes (such as vision, healing, and bone growth) working properly. (c)(i) Lack of vitamin C causes scurvy. (ii) Lack of protein causes kwashiorkor.

questions.questionText: (5 marks): (a) State whether the price will be high or low in the following situations: (i) many bananas but few buyers [1]; (ii) few eggs and many buyers [1]. (b) Give one advantage of growing tomatoes under irrigation in the dry season [1]. (c) Give any two disadvantages of using very old farm machinery [2]
questions.explanation: Model answer. (a)(i) The price will be LOW, because a high supply combined with low demand pushes prices down. (ii) The price will be HIGH, because a low supply combined with high demand pushes prices up. (b) Growing tomatoes under irrigation in the dry season allows the farmer to sell when there is little competition/supply from other rain-fed farmers, so the tomatoes fetch a much higher price. (c) Any two: old machinery breaks down frequently, causing delays; repair and spare parts costs are high; old machinery is often less fuel-efficient, increasing running costs; it may be less safe to operate.

questions.questionText: SECTION B (20 marks - answer any TWO of questions 7 to 10, about 45 minutes). Question 7 (about 10 marks): (a) Complete a table on causes of plant damage and their control, for: (i) veld fires; (ii) pests; (iii) waterlogging [3]. (b) What are the effects of the following on crops: (i) diseases [2]; (ii) drought? [2]. (c) Describe three ways of controlling soil erosion in a crop field [3]
questions.explanation: Model answer. (a)(i) Veld fires - Control: construct firebreaks/firelines around fields, avoid burning veld during the dry season, report and quickly extinguish uncontrolled fires. (ii) Pests - Control: use of pesticides, crop rotation, use of resistant varieties, biological control using natural predators. (iii) Waterlogging - Control: dig drainage channels, plant on raised ridges/beds, avoid over-irrigating. (b)(i) Diseases can stunt plant growth, reduce yield and quality of produce, and in severe cases kill the crop entirely, causing financial loss to the farmer. (ii) Drought causes wilting, poor germination, stunted growth, reduced yields, and can lead to total crop failure if prolonged. (c) Any three: contour ridging/building contour ridges along the slope; planting cover crops or grass strips to bind the soil; practising crop rotation to maintain soil structure; minimum/reduced tillage to avoid disturbing the soil surface unnecessarily; mulching to protect the soil surface from rain impact and wind.

questions.questionText: (about 10-11 marks): (a) Describe five ways of preventing diseases in farm animals [5]. (b) What is an infectious disease? [1]. (c) Describe one infectious disease of farm animals under the following headings: (i) name of disease [1]; (ii) symptoms [2]; (iii) measures for controlling the disease [2]
questions.explanation: Model answer. (a) Any five: regular vaccination of animals; quarantine of newly bought or sick animals before mixing them with the herd; keeping animal housing/kraals clean and well-ventilated; providing a balanced, nutritious diet to boost the animals' immunity; regular dipping/spraying to control ticks and other disease-carrying parasites; avoiding overcrowding of animals; prompt isolation and treatment of any animal showing signs of illness. (b) An infectious disease is a disease that is caused by harmful organisms (such as bacteria, viruses or parasites) and can be spread from one animal to another. (c) Example: (i) Foot and mouth disease. (ii) Symptoms: blisters/sores in the mouth and on the feet, excessive salivation/drooling, lameness, loss of appetite, fever. (iii) Control measures: quarantine and movement restrictions on affected animals, vaccination programmes, disinfecting farm equipment and vehicles, reporting outbreaks immediately to veterinary authorities.

questions.questionText: (about 10 marks): (a) Describe the following: (i) afforestation [1]; (ii) deforestation [1]. (b) Describe the establishment of a woodlot under the following headings: (i) site selection [3]; (ii) planting [2]; (iii) maintenance/care of young trees [3]
questions.explanation: Model answer. (a)(i) Afforestation is the planting of trees on land that did not previously have forest, to establish a new area of woodland. (ii) Deforestation is the cutting down and clearing of trees/forests, usually without adequate replanting. (b)(i) Site selection: choose land with suitable soil depth and drainage for the tree species chosen; consider proximity to a water source for watering young trees; avoid sites prone to waterlogging or severe erosion; consider accessibility for future harvesting/management. (ii) Planting: dig planting holes of an appropriate size and spacing for the species; plant during the rainy season to aid establishment; water the seedlings immediately after planting; firm the soil around the base of each seedling. (iii) Maintenance/care: regular watering during dry spells especially in the first year; weeding around young trees to reduce competition for nutrients and water; protecting seedlings from livestock and fire using fencing or firebreaks; applying mulch to conserve soil moisture; replacing any seedlings that die (beating up).

questions.questionText: (10 marks): A farmer recorded the following business activities in a season: Bought 30kg of vegetable seed for $90; Bought 8 bags of fertiliser at $25 each; Bought chemicals for $45; Sold 800 bundles of vegetables at $2 for 5 bundles; Sold 12 bags of 50kg maize at $18 each. (a) Calculate the total expenses [3]. (b) Calculate the total returns (income) [3]. (c) Calculate the profit or loss made by the farmer [2]. (d) Give two advantages of a farmer selling produce directly to consumers rather than through a middleman [2]
questions.explanation: Model answer, verified by calculation. (a) Total expenses: seed $90 + fertiliser (8 x $25 = $200) + chemicals $45 = 90 + 200 + 45 = $335. (b) Total returns: vegetables - 800 bundles at $2 for every 5 bundles means 800/5 = 160 lots, so 160 x $2 = $320; maize - 12 bags x $18 = $216; Total income = 320 + 216 = $536. (c) Profit = total income - total expenses = 536 - 335 = $201 profit. (d) Any two advantages of selling directly to consumers: the farmer keeps the full/higher selling price instead of losing a share to a middleman's commission/mark-up; the farmer receives payment immediately/faster rather than waiting for a middleman to resell the goods; the farmer builds direct relationships and repeat customers; the farmer has better control over the final selling price.

questions.questionText:
A farmer notices that the topsoil is being washed away after heavy rain.
- (a) Name the process taking place. [1 mark]
- (b) State two causes of the problem. [2 marks]
- (c) Give two methods of controlling it. [2 marks]
questions.explanation: (a) Soil erosion (sheet/water erosion) [1 mark]. (b) Heavy rainfall on bare soil; overgrazing or cultivating down slopes [2 marks]. (c) Contour ploughing/ridging; mulching or planting cover grass [2 marks].

questions.questionText:
A school starts a compost heap using crop residues and kitchen waste.
- (a) Define compost. [1 mark]
- (b) State two materials that can be composted. [2 marks]
- (c) Explain why water is added during compost making. [2 marks]
questions.explanation: (a) Decayed organic matter made from plant and kitchen wastes used as fertiliser [1 mark]. (b) Dry leaves/grass, vegetable peelings, cattle/poultry manure [2 marks]. (c) Moisture supports microorganisms (bacteria/fungi) that break down organic matter and controls heap temperature [2 marks].

questions.questionText:
A farmer grows maize and keeps cattle on the same farm.
- (a) Name the type of farming enterprise involving both crops and livestock. [1 mark]
- (b) Give two benefits of integrating crops and livestock. [2 marks]
- (c) Explain how manure can support crop production. [2 marks]
questions.explanation: (a) Mixed farming [1 mark]. (b) Diverse income sources; crop residues feed livestock while animal manure fertilises crops [2 marks]. (c) Animal manure adds nitrogen, phosphorus, potassium, and humus that improve soil structure and crop yields [2 marks].

questions.questionText:
A farmer plans to irrigate vegetables during a dry period.
- (a) Name one irrigation method. [1 mark]
- (b) State two advantages of irrigation. [2 marks]
- (c) Explain one risk of poor irrigation management. [2 marks]
questions.explanation: (a) Drip irrigation / sprinkler irrigation / furrow irrigation [1 mark]. (b) Enables year-round cropping; increases crop yields during dry spells [2 marks]. (c) Over-irrigation causes waterlogging, leaching of nutrients, and root rot [2 marks].

questions.questionText:
A farmer keeps dairy cattle.
- (a) What is dairy farming? [1 mark]
- (b) State two requirements for healthy dairy cattle. [2 marks]
- (c) Explain why clean water is important. [2 marks]
questions.explanation: (a) Keeping cattle specifically for milk production [1 mark]. (b) Balanced nutritious feed/fodder; clean dry housing and regular dipping/vaccination [2 marks]. (c) Milk is ~87% water, so clean drinking water is essential for milk yield, digestion, and preventing disease [2 marks].

questions.questionText:
A crop is attacked by insects.
- (a) Define a pest. [1 mark]
- (b) Name two methods of pest control. [2 marks]
- (c) Explain why integrated pest management can be useful. [2 marks]
questions.explanation: (a) Any organism (insect, mite, rodent, weed, pathogen) that damages crops or reduces yields [1 mark]. (b) Chemical spraying (pesticides); biological control / crop rotation [2 marks]. (c) Combines cultural, biological, and targeted chemical controls to reduce costs, pesticide resistance, and environmental pollution [2 marks].

questions.questionText:
A farmer wants to improve soil fertility.
- (a) Name one organic manure. [1 mark]
- (b) State two benefits of organic manure. [2 marks]
- (c) Give one precaution when handling manure. [1 mark]
questions.explanation: (a) Kraal manure / compost / chicken droppings [1 mark]. (b) Improves soil structure and water-holding capacity; supplies slow-release nutrients cheaply [2 marks]. (c) Allow fresh manure to decompose/cure so it does not scorch seedlings, and wash hands afterwards [1 mark].

questions.questionText:
A farmer stores harvested grain for several months.
- (a) State one condition required for safe grain storage. [1 mark]
- (b) Name two storage pests or problems. [2 marks]
- (c) Give two ways of reducing storage losses. [2 marks]
questions.explanation: (a) Dry grain (low moisture content ~12%) in a cool, well-ventilated, waterproof store [1 mark]. (b) Maize weevils, larger grain borer, rodents/rats, mould fungi [2 marks]. (c) Hermetic storage bags/metal silos; dusting grain with recommended grain protectant and keeping granaries clean [2 marks].

questions.questionText:
A herd of cattle is grazing continuously in one small area.
- (a) Name the problem that may result. [1 mark]
- (b) State two effects of overgrazing. [2 marks]
- (c) Suggest two grazing-management measures. [2 marks]
questions.explanation: (a) Overgrazing [1 mark]. (b) Loss of grass cover and palatable species; soil compaction and severe soil erosion [2 marks]. (c) Rotational grazing (paddocking); matching stocking rate to carrying capacity [2 marks].

questions.questionText:
A farmer wants to reduce livestock disease.
- (a) Name one disease-prevention measure. [1 mark]
- (b) State two hygiene practices. [2 marks]
- (c) Explain the value of vaccination. [2 marks]
questions.explanation: (a) Vaccination / regular dipping / quarantine [1 mark]. (b) Regular cleaning and disinfection of kraals/fowl runs; providing clean feeders and water troughs [2 marks]. (c) Stimulates immunity against killer diseases (e.g., anthrax, blackleg, Newcastle disease) before outbreaks occur [2 marks].

questions.questionText:
A farmer uses a knapsack sprayer.
- (a) State one use of a knapsack sprayer. [1 mark]
- (b) Name two safety precautions. [2 marks]
- (c) Explain why chemical labels must be followed. [2 marks]
questions.explanation: (a) Applying liquid pesticides, herbicides, or foliar fertilisers onto crops [1 mark]. (b) Wear protective clothing (gloves, mask, goggles, boots); avoid spraying against strong wind [2 marks]. (c) Ensures correct dilution rates, safe pre-harvest intervals, and prevents poisoning or crop burn [2 marks].

questions.questionText:
A farm manager keeps records of sales, inputs and expenses.
- (a) Name the management practice. [1 mark]
- (b) State two benefits of farm records. [2 marks]
- (c) Explain how records help decision-making. [2 marks]
questions.explanation: (a) Farm record keeping [1 mark]. (b) Shows profit or loss clearly; helps track input usage, livestock health, and theft/losses [2 marks]. (c) Enables comparison of enterprise performance to plan future budgets, expand profitable lines, or secure bank loans [2 marks].

questions.questionText:
A farmer wants to reduce financial risk.
- (a) Define risk in farming. [1 mark]
- (b) State two ways of reducing risk. [2 marks]
- (c) Explain the value of diversification. [2 marks]
questions.explanation: (a) Uncertainty of events such as drought, pests, disease, or price drops that can cause financial loss [1 mark]. (b) Enterprise diversification; crop/livestock insurance or irrigation [2 marks]. (c) If one crop fails or drops in price, income from other crops or livestock sustains the farm [2 marks].

questions.questionText:
A farmer selects healthy seeds before planting.
- (a) State one characteristic of good seed. [1 mark]
- (b) Give two reasons for using good seed. [2 marks]
- (c) State one condition needed for germination. [1 mark]
questions.explanation: (a) High germination rate / free from pest damage, weeds, and disease [1 mark]. (b) Produces uniform healthy seedlings and higher yields; prevents introducing weeds or seed-borne diseases [2 marks]. (c) Moisture (water), warmth (suitable temperature), or oxygen [1 mark].

questions.questionText:
A farmer uses crop rotation.
- (a) Define crop rotation. [1 mark]
- (b) State two benefits. [2 marks]
- (c) Explain how rotation can help manage pests or fertility. [2 marks]
questions.explanation: (a) Growing different types of crops in a planned sequence on the same piece of land [1 mark]. (b) Controls soil-borne pests/diseases; maintains balanced soil nutrients and reduces weeds [2 marks]. (c) Legumes (e.g., groundnuts/beans) fix atmospheric nitrogen for following maize crops, while rotating hosts breaks pest life cycles [2 marks].
